en: Good evening. What can I do for you, miss?
Oh dear, that won't do. Let me see
note: Followed by three paused '.' rows (#265), giving 'Let me see...'.

en: Here, isn't this it?
If you don't replace the belt, you'll
drop it in the street again.
I happen to like that belt!
Thaaank you, handsome. Bye!
What a strange girl
Oh, you're the one from earlier
Could it be you came for me...?
Oh! I have to get home. Bye!
<It's a secret>
<I'm a detective>
Oh well, fine. I bet it's way more fun
note: No used_in; inferred reply to the <It's a secret> choice (parallel of #7670).

en: than going to some school, anyway.
Huh?... Are you a student too?
An exchange student? You're kinda my type.
What do you want? And tell me your name.
I'm not a student.
I'm so very ladylike that everyone calls me
"Lady." You can call me that too.
See you, then.
Good day, Mary.
So this big building was a school.
Yep, a school that's no damn fun at all.
Your father is a scholar... How impressive.
Not impressive at all. Papa's obsessed.
He's forever fiddling with weird equations
and gadgets, and he totally ignores me.
What, back again? Going to enroll or what?
Good day, Lady.
You look well. I'm glad to see you.
Wow... aren't you a smooth talker.
But no way, I won't be fooled.
I can't trust handsome men.
, you're the talk of the school.
note: After the name at line start: '{NAME}, you're the talk of the school.'

en: I'm kinda proud I get to talk to you.
Come again. How about a date sometime?
If you're not already spoken for, that is.
Who are you, mister? A pushy peddler?
I assure you I'm nobody suspicious.
is my name, miss.
note: After the name at line start: '{NAME} is my name, miss.'

en: I came to the wrong house. Sorry.
Seems she got the wrong idea.
You're a pushy peddler, right?
Oh, back again? No pushy peddlers.
Father's battling his research. No visitors.
If you want to see me, come to the school. Bye.
I told you, I've got no room to breathe!
My life is ruled by homework.
Come again. Let's talk about all sorts.
, you're always welcome.
note: After the name at line start.

en: Sorry I was such a brat at first.
Would you say, 'I'm sure you can'?
note: Joined directly after #7743, whose variant for msg 301356 (slice 096) ends with a space.

en: Mary
Sleeping so soundly
in my arms
May you grow into a graceful lady
I'll never see you so full of life again.
Forgive me
I am your loyal servant.
Weird... when I woke up, my pillow was at my feet.
I'll obey anything. Now, your orders...
I dreamed of a huge fight in town at night.
Both of us were as strong as monsters!
No, I was just impressed you're up so early,
that's all. Sorry to bother you.
No, I don't mind at all.
Thank you for greeting me.
My name is Mike.
What a polite boy. I'm impressed.
No, it's only natural.
...I don't want to be like my father.
Oh, well, excuse me.
Please don't mind what happened earlier.
Thank you for your hard work again today.
I'll work hard at my studies at school, too.
, you're always
note: After the name at line start; #7839 continues on the next line.

en: so admirable.
